decision: No concrete new source correctness defect identified under valid live single-threaded typed Anchor invocation assumptions. Fresh root build, no-loss scoring and finite runtime acceptance remain separate gates.
scope: Read-only source and pinned local standard-library/Anchor contracts. No private oracle, compiler, VM or source mutation performed for this peer review.
semantic_findings: Original sharing_config.to_account_info() dispatches through blanket ToAccountInfo to as_ref().clone(). The replacement copies all eight AccountInfo fields and clones its lamports and data Rc exactly once; owner is copied last through an aligned read_volatile of the owner field itself. There is no guessed AccountInfo field offset or reference lifetime extension.

The moved event-authority data clone is the concrete default-Global Rc<RefCell<&mut [u8]>>. RefCell<&mut [u8]> is Sized; neither the underlying mutable slice nor the RefCell borrow flag is copied or borrowed by this operation. The added code uses public into_raw/increment_strong_count/from_raw APIs rather than manually assuming an allocation-header offset.

ptr::read creates a temporary uncounted duplicate of the event-authority data handle while the original Rc remains owned by the live account. strong_count and read_volatile cannot invoke user callbacks or unwind in the reviewed valid context; into_raw consumes/forgets the duplicate, increment_strong_count adds exactly one owner using that same raw pointer, and from_raw restores exactly one owned handle.

The source declares ead without initialization but assigns it in the sharing_config owner initializer before the later event_authority data field consumes it. Rust struct expression operands evaluate in written order; no branch reaches event_authority.data without owner initializer completion. The value moves once, so no duplicated Rc destructor is introduced.

After full account context construction, the owned event_authority AccountInfo is dropped normally on CPI success or a returned CPI error. Its data Rc balances the one added strong count. On the pinned Rc overflow path the clone aborts without unwinding, as the original clone does; no fallible result propagation or allocator callback occurs between the transient duplicate and increment.

Only a reference-valued owner load is moved within a reference-counting window. Between the old and new locations there is no CPI, account mutation or payload access that changes the owner. The same sharing_config owner reference and same event-authority Rc allocation reach the CPI. No instruction discriminator, account metadata, signer/writable flags, balances, authorization guard, serialization or field contents are intentionally changed.
assumptions_and_limits: Both source account Rc handles and owner references must be initialized, aligned and live; count is positive because the original strong owner remains alive. Forged/dangling Rc values, unsynchronized access and arbitrary invalid host contexts are excluded.

The manual temporary-handle sequence relies on no unwind/callback between ptr::read and balanced increment/from_raw; this holds for the actual operations reviewed here. Broader generic allocator or callback variants are not qualified.

This new data-clone site introduces no manual private Rc-header arithmetic. Other previously selected weighted Rc/header and Anchor Program shims retain their own pinned-layout assumptions; this review does not re-prove them.

No formal unsafe-Rust equivalence, exhaustive input coverage, historical source attribution, whole Pump ELF identity or token gain is established by this read-only review. Root fresh linked-image and finite signed-runtime checks qualify those separate measurements.
